name: ADUM1281ARZ-RL7
title: ADuM1280/ADuM1281/ADuM1285/ADuM1286: 3 kV rms dual-channel digital isolators, SOIC-8
summary: Two-channel digital isolators built on transformer coupling, rated 3000 V rms for one minute. ADuM1280 and ADuM1285 pass both channels one way; ADuM1281 and ADuM1286 pass one channel each way. ADuM1280/1281 outputs default high and ADuM1285/1286 default low while the input side is unpowered. Grades A, B and C run to 1, 25 and 100 Mbps; each side takes 2.7 V to 5.5 V (W grades 3.0 V to 5.5 V), from −40°C to +125°C. ADUM1281ARZ-RL7 is the 1 Mbps, one-each-way, default-high part on tape and reel.

operation.text: Each part carries two independent isolated channels. ADuM1280 and ADuM1285 send both channels from side 1 to side 2; ADuM1281 and ADuM1286 send channel B from side 1 to side 2 and channel A from side 2 to side 1. Grades A, B and C set the maximum data rate at 1, 25 and 100 Mbps.
When the input side is unpowered, or not yet powered at start-up, the outputs of ADuM1280 and ADuM1281 sit high and those of ADuM1285 and ADuM1286 sit low.

Each side has its own supply and ground. Industrial grades run each side from 2.7 V to 5.5 V and automotive W grades from 3.0 V to 5.5 V, so the two sides may sit at different voltages and the part translates logic levels between 3 V and 5 V systems.

Each input edge sends a pulse of about 1 ns across a transformer to a bistable decoder, which the pulse sets or resets. If the input holds still for longer than about 1.6 µs, refresh pulses carrying the present input state go out periodically to keep the output correct at DC. If the decoder sees no pulse for more than about 6.4 µs it treats the input side as unpowered or failed, and a watchdog forces the output to its default state.

An external field disturbs the part only if it induces enough voltage in the receiving coil to set or reset the decoder falsely. Transformer output pulses exceed 1.5 V against a decoder threshold near 1.0 V, a 0.5 V margin. The allowable field and allowable nearby current curves are worked out for ADuM1280 at 3 V, the most susceptible case, holding the induced voltage to half that margin. At 1 MHz the allowable field is 0.08 kgauss, which induces 0.25 V in the receiving coil; at the same frequency a 0.2 kA current 5 mm from the part is needed to affect operation. Strong high-frequency fields can also induce error voltages in loops formed by PCB traces that trip following circuitry, so trace loops are to be avoided.

The logic pins need no external interface parts. Both supply pins, VDD1 and VDD2, take a bypass capacitor of 0.01 µF to 0.1 µF, with no more than 20 mm of total lead length between the capacitor's two ends and the supply pin.

Unshielded, with a suitable PCB, the part can pass the radiated emission limits of CISPR 22 and FCC at Class A and also the tighter Class B. Layout and stack-up guidance is in Analog Devices application note AN-1109.

Propagation delay runs from the input crossing 50% to the output crossing 50%; tPLH and tPHL can differ. Pulse width distortion is the largest difference between tPLH and tPHL. Channel-to-channel matching is the largest delay difference between the two channels of one part, specified separately for codirectional and opposing-direction channels. Propagation delay skew is the largest delay difference between separate units under the same conditions.

Current drawn by a channel depends on supply voltage, data rate and output load. Below half the refresh rate each channel draws its quiescent current; above it the current rises with data rate. Total VDD1 and VDD2 current is the sum of the input and output channel currents on each side.

Insulation wears out under long voltage stress at a rate that depends on the waveform. Bipolar AC is the hardest case and sets the recommended working voltage of 565 V peak for a 50-year minimum life. Unipolar AC and DC stress the barrier less, so higher working voltages still give 50 years. A unipolar waveform may be of either polarity but never crosses 0 V; any waveform that does cross 0 V is to be treated as bipolar and held to the bipolar limit. Approved working voltages above the 50-year figure can shorten insulation life.
